subject: BridgePay POC: scope, success criteria, and model shortlist
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@bridgepay.com>, Ethan Rodriguez <ethan@bridgepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: BridgePay POC: scope, success criteria, and model shortlist

Hi Maya / Ethan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we can align on a pilot that proves the integration and the economics you care about. I tried to keep this lean — please flag anything missing.

Summary of goals (from your team):
- Increase merchant chat resolution rate for billing and refunds from ~72% -> target 88% automated resolution (deflection)
- Maintain SLA: median response time under 500ms for live agents assisted flows
- Support EN / ES / PT (English, Spanish, Portuguese) with parity on high-confidence responses
- Keep per-session inference cost below $0.45 for the sampled workload

Proposed POC scope (4 weeks):
1) Week 0: Kickoff & access — share data samples, create sandbox API keys, Q/A on privacy expectations
2) Week 1–2: Integration & baseline — wire up chat logs to Redwood sandbox; run baseline metrics on current rule-based bot + small LLM baseline
3) Week 3: Model evaluation runs — run shortlisted models on representative prompt set and gather latency/cost/quality metrics
4) Week 4: Acceptance test & handoff — run acceptance prompts and produce final scorecard + recommended runtime configs

Model shortlist (our recommendation for trial):
- Primary model: Starling-FT-13B (open-weights fine-tuned for instruction + commerce dialogue). Good latency/cost balance for EN, has competitive ES performance with prompt adapters.
- Fallback: Llama2-70B-quant (quantized variant) — higher quality on edge cases, used only for hard-fail paths or low-throughput offline rerank jobs.
- Multilingual adapter: small language-specific adapter for ES/PT (to be layered on Starling-FT) — reduces hallucination on regional billing terms.

Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Automated resolution >= 85% on accepted test set (close to your 88% target; we can tune prompts/thresholds to hit the higher target in production)
- Median per-request latency <= 500ms under a 20 RPS simulated load
- End-to-end per-session inference cost < $0.45 on the sampled traffic profile
- No PII exfiltration incidents in randomized privacy checks (we will run the Redwood data-checker on logs)

Owners & responsibilities:
- Redwood (Soojin + Priyom): POC orchestration, model runs, evaluation matrix, short adapters and runbook.
- Redwood (Ben): commercial contact, pricing and procurement coordination.
- BridgePay (Maya): dataset access, acceptance test set, success signoff.
- BridgePay (Ethan): engineering lead for integration and sandbox keys.

Next steps / asks from BridgePay:
1) Share sample conversation logs (anonymized) and the acceptance test set by Tue 11/13
2) Confirm that BridgePay legal is OK with the sandbox access model (we can provide a privacy brief)
3) Confirm target go/no-go date for production launch (we recommended Dec 20 but open to your schedule)

Attachments: attached a one-pager evaluation matrix and our quickstart YAML for sandbox deploy.

If you're good with this, we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff next week (please share 2 slots).

Thanks —

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions (West)
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: Maya Singh <maya@bridgepay.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Nov 2028 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BridgePay POC: scope, success criteria, and model shortlist

Thanks Soojin — this is super helpful and tracks with what we discussed. A few quick notes from our side:

1) Dataset: we can deliver 2 weeks of anonymized chat + 1 week of high-touch escalations by Tue 11/14. Will need an NDA addendum (we emailed procurement).
2) Multilingual: Spanish is the most critical for now; Portuguese is lower priority but would be nice to see parity later. If Starling-FT can hit ~80–82% on ES out of the box, that would be acceptable for the trial.
3) Latency: 500ms median is firm for the assisted agent path. If you anticipate issues, we need to understand fallback behavior (e.g., route to lighter model vs send to agent).

Questions:
- What telemetry will you need from our side to compute per-session cost accurately? (tokenization profile, average prompt size?)
- Can you confirm who will own adapter fine-tuning for ES? We prefer Redwood to own it during the POC.

We'd like to do kickoff on Wed 11/15 at 11:00 PT if that works for your team.

—Maya
Sr. PM, Merchant Experience
BridgePay

Forwarding a quick internal note after syncing with infra:

- ES adapter plan: we can produce an ES adapter prototype in 5 business days after we receive the anonymized 2-week sample. Prototype = adapter weights + automated validation harness showing top-1 fidelity improvement on localized billing terms.
- Runs & infra: to hit 500ms median at 20 RPS for Starling-FT-13B, we'll use a combination of batching + pre-warmed instances and the prefix-KV cache for sticky merchants. Expect a ~12% latency improvement vs a cold continuous-run.
- Deliverables by end of Week 3: per-model CSV with latency/cost/acceptance-score, adapter artifact, recommended runtime YAML for Redwood Dedicated/Hosted options.

I'll own the model runs and artifact handoff. Ben — please loop procurement for the POC credit doc and I'll coordinate the tracker for run params.
